subject: boss-debt-bearer
label: The Debt-Bearer — Barbarian champion, tower floor 1, fire
provenance: Design is Raheem's. He took my Leonardo concept and edited it through eight
passes in the Leonardo web app; the final one ('Pull the weapons and halo
some') was recovered via the Leonardo API to bg-harness/refs/debt-bearer/.
The reference is a CROP of that image with the rune-weapon ring removed. The
ring must never be baked into the sprite — it ships as a separate effect
layer so its weapons can detach and fly as attacks resolve. Baked in, it is
welded to the character forever and can only ever spin as one piece.
Approved by Raheem 2026-07-30 before any generation was spent.
description: A hulking misshapen monster in heavy dark iron plate armour covering it completely from neck to feet, with enormous hunched shoulders far wider than its hips, no neck, a heavy grey brute head with a wide tusked jaw and burning white-hot eyes, long thick arms and clawed hands. Molten orange fire glows through cracks in its armour plates, a burning fire core at its belt, and flames burn around its feet. Dark iron grey, soot black and oxblood with bright orange fire. Standing, facing the viewer.
animationNotes: v3, not pro and not template.
pro    — the only mode whose mechanism prevents cross-frame drift, but it
cost ~46 generations PER DIRECTION on hero-chibi v1 and still
returned corrupt frames. ~280 generations for one boss.
template — cheap, but it LOST THE SOUTH FACING on a previous run and
returned the back of the head. For a frontal boss that is total
loss. The mannequin template list also has no 'attack'.
v3     — ~3 generations per direction, passed the gate first try.
Every clip pins custom_start_frame to the SAME rot-south.png. That makes one
rotation the single identity anchor for the whole set, so the clips cannot
drift away from each other, and it gives a free exact check: frame 0 of every
clip must come back near-identical to that file.
frameCount is what we ASK for; v3 returns frameCount + 1, frame 0 being the
pinned pose. So 3 -> 4 frames, 7 -> 8 frames. Getting this wrong does not
error, it just makes every clip one frame longer than the manifest claims.
Costume nouns are repeated verbatim from the character description on purpose
— saying 'armour' in one clip and 'iron plate' in another invites the model to
redecorate between clips.
M5.7: every pose keeps the figure covered neck to feet. No 'chest heaving',
no 'armour breaking away', no bare-torso 'unleashed' phase-2 silhouette —
those are standard generator drift for charge and enrage poses.

animations.name: idle
animations.action: standing still, breathing slowly, heavy shoulders in dark iron plate armour rising and falling, arms hanging at its sides, feet planted, facing the viewer
animations.note: 4 is the API MINIMUM (frame_count >= 4, rejected 3 with a 422 before spending anything), so this returns 5 frames. At fps 3 that is a 1667ms breath cycle — slow, which is right for something this heavy. The single most important clip: a boss that never breathes reads as floating, which is the whole reason this work exists.

animations.name: windup
animations.action: slowly lifting both long clawed arms upward and back above its head, elbows bending, heavy iron plate shoulders rotating up, body leaning back, ending with both fists raised high overhead, facing the viewer
animations.note: LOOPS and HOLDS while the telegraph is on screen — a charge can span several hero turns, so this has to be watchable for an unknown length of time. Ends on the raised-fists pose that 'smash' begins from.

animations.name: smash
animations.action: swinging both raised fists downward through a wide arc and striking the ground in front of it, arms ending low and crossed near the ground, body hunched forward over the impact, facing the viewer
animations.note: ONE action, not three. The first attempt asked for 'raising AND smashing down AND recovering' in a single clip and the model rendered none of the arm motion — it just erupted in fire and returned to standing. Splitting the raise into 'windup' leaves this clip a single unambiguous arc. Chained from the wind-up's last frame so the strike starts with the arms already up.

animations.name: attack
animations.action: raising both long clawed arms high overhead and smashing them down forward toward the viewer, heavy iron plate armour shifting with the swing, then recovering to a planted stance, facing the viewer
animations.note: frame_count must be EVEN and >= 4 (4,6,8,10,12,14,16) — 7 was rejected 422 before any spend. ~8 frames at 12fps = 667ms, which fits windUpNormal(250) + impact(400) = 650ms with slack. Sized to the NORMAL beat: sizing to the heavy beat would truncate every ordinary attack mid-swing. MEASURE the returned frame count, do not assume it equals what was asked.

animations.name: hit
animations.action: recoiling backward from a heavy blow to the chest, head snapping back, shoulders twisting, heavy iron plate armour absorbing the impact, feet planted, facing the viewer
animations.note: 5 frames at 8fps = 625ms against a 400ms impact beat; it lands the flinch and holds the recovery.

animations.name: rage
animations.action: standing more heavily and more still, shoulders lowered, head raised, the fire in the cracks of its dark iron plate armour burning brighter and steadier, arms hanging loose at its sides, facing the viewer
animations.note: RETIRED. Measured 7.65 peak mean-abs-diff between frames — LESS than idle's 8.22, i.e. a differently-named idle. The description ('more still, fire steadier') gave the model nothing to move.

animations.name: defeat
animations.action: staggering backward, then dropping heavily onto one knee with its head bowed, fire dimming in the cracks of its armour, facing the viewer
animations.note: Ends on one knee rather than prone — a ledger-keeper stops, he does not sprawl.

animations.name: ultimate
animations.action: hunching forward and drawing both long clawed arms inward across its chest as fire gathers and brightens in the burning core at its belt, heavy iron plate armour fully covering it, gathering power, facing the viewer
animations.note: LOOPS under the 3000ms ultimate beat — a one-shot would freeze the boss for two seconds at the most dramatic moment in the fight. Armour explicitly named as staying ON: 'gathering power' poses are exactly where generators try to strip a figure (M5.7).

animations.name: ablaze
animations.action: standing squared and motionless with its head raised and arms loose at its sides, while bright fire pours upward out of every crack in its heavy dark iron plate armour and burns fiercely around its shoulders and arms, armour fully covering it from neck to feet, facing the viewer
animations.note: Phase-2 resting pose, replacing 'rage'. The change has to be in the FIRE, not the stance: the lore is 'the counting stops, he has reached the total', so he goes blazing and STILL rather than thrashing — which is also how it avoids Barbarian §14's ban on generic-rage vocabulary. Names the armour as covering because 'fire pours out of him' is exactly the phrasing that makes a generator strip a figure (M5.7).
